name: 銀ダラの西京焼き (Gindara no Saikyō-yaki) · Miso-Glazed Black Cod
description: Nobu's famous dish, from the old Kyoto tradition of saikyo-yaki: black cod cured for 2 to 3 days in sweet white miso, sake and mirin, then broiled until caramelized and finished in the oven. Serves 4.

ingredients.text: 4 black cod (sablefish) fillets, about 170 g each, skin on
ingredients.item: black cod (sablefish) fillets, about 170 g each, skin on

ingredients.text: 180 g white miso (saikyo miso if possible)
4 hajikami (pickled ginger shoots) or pickled ginger, to serve
ingredients.item: hajikami (pickled ginger shoots) or pickled ginger, to serve

steps.text: Bring 60 ml sake and 60 ml mirin to a boil in a saucepan and boil 20 seconds to cook off the alcohol. Turn the heat to low and whisk in 180 g white miso (saikyo miso if possible) until smooth. Raise the heat, add 90 g sugar and stir until it dissolves, about 1 minute. Cool completely.
Sprinkle 4 black cod (sablefish) fillets, about 170 g each, skin on lightly with 1/2 tsp salt, leave 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Spread a third of the marinade in a dish, lay in the fish and cover with the rest. Cover tightly and refrigerate 2 to 3 days.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Wipe the excess marinade off the fish with your fingers and paper towels; don't rinse it.
Broil the fillets skin side down on an oiled rack 15 cm from the heat for 4 minutes, until the top is browned and blackened in spots.
Move to the middle of the oven and bake 10 minutes, until the fish flakes and is just opaque.
Serve with 4 hajikami (pickled ginger shoots) or pickled ginger, to serve.

notes:
The salting step and 2 to 3 day cure season the fish all the way through and firm its texture. One day works but is milder. Watch the broiler closely: the sugar in the miso goes from caramelized to burnt fast.

Black cod (sablefish) is rich enough to stay silky; salmon, Chilean sea bass or mackerel work too, with 1 day of cure. Leftover marinade keeps a week for a second batch.
